text: Chapter 1: Introduction presents the research background, motivation, problem statement, thesis statement, objectives, research questions and hypotheses, scope, and limitations.

Chapter 2: Literature Review reviews prior research on BGP operation, routing incidents, anomaly detection, routing security, AS relationships, RPKI/ROV, and machine-learning approaches relevant to BGP incident analysis.

Chapter 3: Methodology describes the incident dataset, data partitioning, RouteViews data collection, five-minute analytical windows, behavioral feature engineering, CAIDA and RPKI/ROV enrichment, model-development strategy, leakage controls, incident-level stacking architecture, and evaluation methodology.

Chapter 4: Results presents the baseline experiments, imbalance analysis, feature ablation, Random Forest and XGBoost comparisons, Validation results, incident-level stacking experiments, forensic verification, and Final Holdout classification and ranking performance.

Chapter 5: Conclusions discusses the major findings, practical implications for enterprise network operations, study limitations, contributions, and recommendations for future research, including real-time and streaming extensions.
